Summary
Data source overview:  
The paper introduces the Interactive System Optimizer (ISO), a two-stage algorithm that (1) infers a reward function directly from user interaction logs via Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) and (2) repeatedly re-optimises the interactive system with Reinforcement Learning (RL) so that users gradually receive higher utility. Extensive simulations on 40 synthetic systems show large gains in expected user value, especially when the recovered reward signal is accurate.

Inference strategy justification:  
The paper is heavy on methodology. To construct causal-interventional pathways we decomposed ISO into its white-box sub-components (reward inference, MDP transformation, RL optimisation) and created separate nodes for the empirical findings about convergence behaviour. Interventions were split into “Deploy ISO” (full pipeline) and the narrower “Apply MaxEnt-IRL” step, because many other papers will mention MaxEnt-IRL and those nodes must merge cleanly across the 500 k-source graph.

Extraction completeness explanation:  
16 tightly-connected nodes (≈15/5 000 w guideline) capture all reasoning steps from the top-level risk (“objective misalignment”) through root causes, insights, design rationales, mechanisms, validation and finally to actionable interventions. Every node is referenced by ≥1 edge; no isolated nodes remain.

Key limitations:  
1. Results are simulation-only, so edge confidence is at most 3-4.  
2. No real-world deployment yet; intervention maturity set to “2 Experimental”.  
3. Some moderate inference was required to phrase safety-relevant risks explicitly.

EXTRACTION_CONFIDENCE[87]

Instruction-set improvement suggestion:  
Provide explicit examples showing how to deal with purely methodological papers (where “risks” are implicit utility failures) and clarify preferred edge verb between “problem analysis” and “theoretical insight” (“addressed_by” vs “mitigated_by”) to reduce ambiguities.
